column3: Vitest snapshot of the Windows caption menubar DOM in English and Chinese (two exports, one per locale).
Tests accountView field projection (drops token/codeVerifier), rejects non-browser authorizeUrl schemes, and drives account Remote commands plus account/watchExpiry over a real WebSocket.
Builds an app.asar with the sandbox-windows-acl package and proves the archived ACL skill still executes under external pwsh and disposes its extracted copy.

DesktopBackendController lifecycle: shares preparation between concurrent starts, waits for pending preparation on close, publishes preparation errors for retry, and never leaves a failed child overlapping a retry.
DesktopBackgroundNotice close-confirmation: keeps the window visible until confirmation, remembers acknowledgement across launches via a marker file, and cancels without recording.
Proves the installed dsh launcher preserves args, cwd, env, stdin bytes, stderr and exit status; on POSIX it resolves chained symlinks without expanding argument contents.
desktopClientVersion refuses to guess a version when DSH_CLIENT_VERSION is absent or empty, and desktopClientMetadata reports version/locale/timezone offset.
Installs/removes the Desktop CLI link with backup-and-restore semantics: preserves foreign npm links, rejects a changed confirmation fingerprint, and serialises simultaneous choices.
presentCommandManagement for en/zh across darwin/win32, including the shadowed-command warning when another dsh takes PATH precedence, and snapshots the dialog JSON.
Crosses a real worker process for CLI install/repair/remove; only the OS mutation boundary is substituted, and AppleScript elevation is exercised without authorising a mutation.
Windows-only: drives the real command-path.ps1 worker against a unique registry key tree to prove unrelated PATH entries are preserved.
Verifies the local desktop package set (integrity, ordering, version match) and rejects registry resolutions for names the local set owns.
Loopback HTTP server that captures the exact bytes, path and headers the real COS SDK sends, redirecting only the URL so the signature stays intact.
Proves cosOperation enforces a TOTAL deadline across SDK retries: aborts a stalled retry, an active download and a pending PUT, and clears the timer after success.
Crash report rendering (facts header, inspected error with properties and cause, renderer console tail), owner-only writes, oldest-first pruning and byte caps.
Resolves the update/upload environment: test deployment default, strict 32-hex release ID, per-target feed and binary prefixes, HTTPS-origin-only download URL, Nightly metadata names.
Build commit/dirty round-trip through the child environment plus the desktop toolchain preflight (tar, vswhere) which writes nothing into the working directory.
Every mutable build directory is isolated per target while only the immutable upstream download cache is shared; target-to-platform mapping and env overrides.
Derives the next build-version suffix by scanning existing artifacts (including -unnotarized/-unsigned variants) and ignoring other dates or product versions.
Validates build versions: must extend the product prerelease, no build metadata, stable bases open a -test. prefix, and artefacts normalise a leading v.
A rolldown plugin that fails the bundle when a static, dynamic or require() import is not shipped by the packaged app, with a separate Node-builtin policy for the sandboxed preload.
The installed CLI dispatches with the bundled pnpm distribution and Electron's package-operation environment even when PATH is absent.
Local packaging configuration per platform file: unsigned public settings, cache concurrency, release-ID ownership, mandatory-update origins, npm mirror rules, macOS signing identity checks.
Selects the exact successful packaging attempt and its registered runner, rejects mismatched evidence without falling back, and resolves an old locally retained release.
Mandatory-update policy environment: selects test/production origin and auth together, rejects non-HTTPS or credentialed origins, and forbids allowedAuthOrigins in production.
Publication failure classification keeps actionable validation and filesystem diagnostics while dropping provider bodies, unknown messages and raw SDK errors.
Preflights a complete retained build without credentials, re-verifies signatures after approval, and refuses a changed file, wrong machine or changed approval digest.
Renders the human-readable approval summary with upload-byte fingerprints and escapes runner display text so it cannot add Markdown rows or HTML elements.
Reads public publish settings without opening the absent credential file, requires the GitHub App configuration for production, and rejects multiline App outputs.
Real COS SDK over the loopback origin: overwrite-prevention header, streamed verified bytes, readback hashing, 1 MiB channel cap, and safe denial receipts.
Preflight rejects unnotarized/unsigned artifacts from paginated GitHub artifact metadata and refuses malformed package_run_id before any API call.
Cross-process channel lock (one writer per channel) plus an audit journal that persists intent, before/after bytes and terminal state outside the checkout.
Routes the exact successful attempt to its registered machine, failing closed on missing/duplicate runner labels and rejecting repository-branch packages for production.
Publishes the release tag with explicit App authentication: idempotent when present, refuses to move a conflicting tag, and reconciles a create race with a 422.
Publish order (binaries then feed), identical bytes skipped, ambiguous write recovery without repeating it, published-tag-pending state, and conflict/superseded stops with no writes.
Retained release store: one writer per attempt, changed-byte detection, incomplete copies never exposed, and manifest identity/inventory tampering rejected.
git tag/push flow for desktop-v<version>: refuses to move a tag naming another commit, reports git failures without throwing, and offers explicit recovery commands.
Channel rollback previews the exact YAML change before any write, verifies the historical binary first, and resumes a partially restored nightly/latest pair.
Builds the upload plan: latest installer per deployment, per-target objects and YAML inside the test release directory, blockmap validation, and channel metadata published last.
Real COS SDK upload run against the loopback origin: retains plan, feed bytes, intent, receipt and hashes; a failed PUT is not retried and raw SDK diagnostics are excluded.
Cold-start launcher passes literal workspace paths and devtools flags to Electron without evaluating shell syntax.
Development runtime inventory includes unhoisted workspace packages; plugin management does not modify linked packages; a CLI package from another release is rejected.
readDeviceInfo emits one line per available fact and omits (rather than fails on) a field whose source is absent or throws.
Directory picker restores/focuses the parent, shares one unanswered dialog, discards a selection after the parent is destroyed, and refuses foreign renderers/frames.

Fatal dialog waits for the crash report to settle, offers exit/restart (plus disable-plugins), never lets a late acknowledgement re-hide the window, and bounds the report deadline.
Loopback server serving real executables through a synthetic Nightly feed with correct SHA-512 and optional transfer corruption, plus Range/differential controls.
Windows console probe that owns a console, launches the CLI child inside a kill-on-close job object and dispatches a console Ctrl event to prove signal delivery.
PowerShell worker using a unique registry key tree to exercise the real Invoke-DshCommandPath install/inspect/remove operations without touching the user environment.
Four-line plugin that exposes the real Loader-composed Host context to the qualification fixture through a promise.
Built-Host qualification: runs the real profile Loader with a held model adapter, installs the update-task control and drives admission locking over the real Host.
PowerShell stub replacing every firewall cmdlet so the network-fault plan can be exercised for creation failure, foreign rule, declined confirmation and restore failure cases.
Inert packaging subprocess that writes a fake installer, blockmap and nightly.yml, or exits non-zero on DSH_TEST_PACKAGING_FAIL.
NSIS smoke that compiles against the production directory transaction, stages and promotes an application, then forces a promote conflict and rolls back.
NSIS smoke comparing direct extraction against extract-then-copy under a locked file, proving exit code 0 alone cannot establish a correct extraction.
Real Electron HTTP/download qualification driving the actual updater, coordinator, mandatory policy and dialogs; installer execution is forbidden and replaced by a recorded observation.
Independent process exercising one signature-cache writer through native TypeScript stripping, synchronising sign/verify through the IPC channel.
Locates the mandatory-update child frame and proxies the parent so mouse events are dispatched at the frame with the Windows titlebar offset.
Creates one-page .docx/.xlsx/.pptx inputs with python-docx/openpyxl/python-pptx for the Office conversion smoke.
Electron-mode smoke proving removeOwnedDirectory deletes the owned tree while preserving a linked directory target and the installed runtime bytes.
Keeps an owned descendant alive and then fails the packaging run, proving the supervisor kills the stage and its descendant.
Real Electron fixture that observes and dismisses the Platform notice across account sign-out/sign-in to prove per-account storage isolation.
Installs and uses a local dependency with the packaged pnpm and Electron Node launcher, asserting no system pnpm is used and the launcher carries --expose-internals.
Exercises the filtered Desktop native/HTML dependencies, node-pty and the packaged pnpm under the Electron Node runtime with a scrubbed environment.
Real Electron download, checksum, Authenticode publisher check and coordinator recovery over the artifact server; installer execution is forbidden.
Child process that tries to take the persistent Windows signing interlock and prints acquired or blocked, without loading a signer.
Real isolated update dialogs served over the dsh-app protocol, exercising cancel and explicit install through the production preload and renderer.
Native overlay qualification with no Host or network: parent hide/show, document readiness and listener cleanup, compared against the owner-local expected output.
Loopback update feed with deterministic transport failures (healthy, stall, feed-stall, corrupt, 404) and request barriers for Electron qualification.
Child that spawns a node-pty terminal and asserts natural exit releases the worker, and that a kill also cleans up.
Independent process that takes the signing stage lock, waits on IPC, and exercises the cache-clear path with a hardware-free signer.
Replaces only the coordinator, host process and error types of the compiled main entry, recording states, installations and task queries for the workspace scenario.
Private token-authenticated HTTP control inside the real Desktop Host to queue/clear a task, hold shutdown and report agent and request state.
Operator control window for the workspace qualification: menus choose ordinary/mandatory updates, hold and release downloads, inject failures and queue or clear tasks.
Real Electron main entry, preload, shared Web Host and local updater with the installer call intercepted; ten automated scenarios plus an interactive mode.
Cross-process file-lock entry helper used by the publishing and packaging locks.
DesktopHostProcess over private IPC: fatal and crash events after readiness, task inspection deadlines, Web authentication URL, platform identity validation and credential clearing on shutdown.
Host task protection: counts running agents, queued turns/steps and global/agent jobs, locks admission for new requests (503), drains existing ones and rechecks tasks.
The generated qualification bootstrap entry assigns isolated user-data/home/journal paths for both versions before loading main, and refuses foreign app identity.
Freezes shipped application bytes once without credentials, rejects modified/added/missing files, and builds an isolated electron-builder config per version.
Qualification COS transport over the loopback origin: streamed PUT with explicit length/MD5/no-store, no retry on an uncertain failure, per-operation deadlines and safe readback hashing.
Plans the two binary sets and the fixed feed URL for two versions, with publication unauthorised, and rejects changed bytes, missing map, foreign URL, wrong version and legacy hash.
Binds the network-fault plan to the verified executable bytes and rejects a failed/wrong-run/wrong-version receipt or a changed, renamed or outside file before creating the plan.
Reads the real ASAR and runtime inventories from an archive, rejecting unsafe archive paths, credential files, changed descriptors and dependency manifests that are not the builder transformation.
The operator packaging entry refuses the signing interlock before loading credentials, strips unrelated secrets, and can check without confirmation or a packaging directory.
Publication sequencing: upload without advertising, publish version 1, require version 1 startup before version 2, and refuse a failed, wrong-version or mismatched upload receipt.

Allocates test-only namespaces and validates journal evidence: ordered milestones, no joining of fragments, a fresh retry after a later failure, and a collection that never claims operator acceptance.
Retags only release-owned packages and dependencies in the copied runtime, preserves third-party versions, and stops after a failed version without a completion receipt.
Read-only signature evidence: hashes actual bytes with the feed algorithm and verifies the installer with the real updater verifier without executing it.
Bilingual pairing record: per-section hashes of the English and Chinese network-fault README blocks.
Operator checklist for blocking and restoring only the installed test application's outbound traffic, with the limits of the Windows firewall evidence.
Chinese version of the network-fault operator checklist.
Bilingual pairing record for the publication README.
Test upload and fixed-feed publication procedure: bucket-versioning prerequisite, per-operation deadlines, receipts reused by feed publication, and the 403 diagnosis by exact API.
Chinese version of the test upload and publication procedure.
Bilingual pairing record for the installed-update walkthrough README.
Operator walkthrough for a Windows installed update: prepare materials, the eight-step operator sequence, evidence and recovery, and an explicit list of what is still unverified.
Chinese version of the installed-update operator walkthrough.
Installer preparation rejects a missing production policy before signing, keeps electron-builder responsible for node_modules, names unsigned artifacts and packages every preload entry.
Keybinding persistence writes into the supplied userData, reloads a null binding, and refuses to rewrite a file written by a future schema version.

The largest spec in the shard: keyboard shortcut registration, native menu accelerators, chord interception, held-key state and browser-guest input routing, including blocking while an update overlay loads.
English and Chinese dictionaries ship the same key set; placeholder formatting leaves unknown placeholders intact; startup locale prefers an explicit choice then the first supported system language.
Passes Apple's rejection JSON back from a nonzero notarytool wait exit so electron-notarize can retrieve the diagnostic, and does not treat failed upload as submission.
Notary submission then wait with separate timings, redacted events.jsonl that never contains the Apple ID or password, and preserved Invalid/Rejected statuses.
Reads the login shell environment via delimited output, merging shell values except probe-session and launcher-owned names, with per-candidate failure records and abort handling.
Resolves and writes the fixed release feed for the generic Nightly provider, and verifies the updater cache directory name inside the signed app.
The macOS signature cache policy key includes certificate, identifier, team, authority, timestamp, runtime flag and entitlements, and rejects each mismatch.
Verifies an unnotarized DMG's signature and identity without Apple notarization tools, and still requires a stapled ticket and Gatekeeper acceptance for a release DMG.
The system-proxy transaction preserves and restores the user's HTTP/HTTPS/PAC settings, refuses unpreservable configurations before mutation, and never steals a live lock.
Runs the codesign/stapler/spctl qualification sequence in order and stops at the first failing command.
Loads the macOS local packaging preset and validates its identity, credentials and cache settings before any Apple credential is used.
Pack concurrency and download/notarization proxies are read from the environment, invalid values are rejected without echoing the proxy, and child proxy variables override the parent.
Signs Mach-O runtime files in place, signs a shared Python interpreter once, and rejects unknown, absolute, escaping, dangling, chained or directory links before signing anything.
The macOS signature cache directory must be an unlinked, private POSIX directory; a 0700 cache is validated and a rebuilt checkout still finds its cached signature.
Cached macOS signatures are reused without shared mutable storage, invalidated by changed input/policy/mode, and never publish or replace the input after a signing or verification failure.
Release signing configuration and identity checks: hardened runtime, secure timestamp, exact authority and team, complete notarization credential strategy, and isolated unsigned artefacts.
Scopes signing to a temporary imported keychain, removes CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD before the build, restores the user's keychain search list, and allocates distinct keychains for overlapping runs.
The real macOS signer walk visits each Framework file once and keeps nested bundle signing, with symlink aliases resolved to distinct real paths.
The shard's largest file (2267 lines): the whole desktop main entry - Host startup, mandatory/ordinary update flows, quit confirmation, crash recovery, platform view and IPC ownership.
Mandatory-update policy client: flattened 40005 handling, bounded backoff with jitter, per-check deadline, block retention across auth expiry, and page-origin validation.
The mandatory-update window: version-bound click approval, deferral, copy/browser fallback, no renderer quit privilege, and Windows overlay publication into the main document.
Media permissions are granted only to the owned primary application frame for audio, and macOS microphone authorisation is asked once and awaited.
desktopNodeEnvironment keeps private Desktop launchers out of the Host environment and supplies them only to package installation processes.
removeOwnedDirectory deletes the owned tree, preserves unknown directory-link targets, unlinks a root link with a missing target and refuses a regular-file root.
Parallel macOS artifact lanes notarize isolated copies, promote only completed payloads, collect both failures, and reject an incomplete qualification step.
A failed packaging stage records redacted parent failures in events.jsonl and result.json without leaking the credential sentinel, and restores the environment.
The staged packaging pipeline: one signing preflight before building, shared storage initialised under the stage lock, no release record on failure, and the Apple proxy scoped to notarization only.
Selects the runtime and electron-builder architecture per target, keeps publishing disabled for the separate upload, and removes ambient certificate or COS credentials from packaging subprocesses.
The after-pack hook requires the product version from the bundled runtime, or the version qualification wrote, and a build version does not change that requirement.

Packaging run records redact credential values across every byte split, keep failed-stage output, kill a stage and its descendant on a fatal marker, and fail closed when the journal cannot be written.
A packaging step redacts nested error causes, records a restored proxy in the summary, and never persists a successful return value.
The sandboxed platform preload exposes a synchronous credential getter after exactly one bootstrap IPC, never to subframes, and fails closed on an issuer mismatch.
Real Chromium storage survives native view and Electron process lifetimes; the built platform-view artifact is imported for the check.
The embedded Platform view: token never in a URL, cross-origin navigation blocked, deployment headers injected only at the Platform origin, per-account partitions and cleanup ordering.
The packaged login placeholder renders its label from the main-process query under a default-src 'none' CSP.
Test Feishu login: isolated memory session, sandboxed window, single F12 DevTools, refused navigation and permissions, and cancellation reported once with a retry allowed.
The application preload exposes each capability only to the right document and frame - onboarding, update status, device info, boot, directory picker, shortcuts and guest input.
The mandatory overlay lives in an in-page frame, accepts actions only through a transferred private port, and closes its channel on navigation.
The Windows caption menubar mounts only after the application frame replaces the loading document, localises entries and restores text selection before opening a menu.
Fullscreen state is mirrored onto html[data-fullscreen] on darwin/win32 and no channel is subscribed on linux.
The native theme source is mirrored to the main process through a MutationObserver, deferred until the document root exists.
Windows appearance (language, titlebar height, palette colours) is synchronised live and observation stops on pagehide.
Built preloads must load with only Electron's sandbox-supported require - no filesystem module access.
Selects the internal production closure for the desktop package set, rejects a required package missing from the packed inputs, and requires both Host and CLI entries.
Runtime patch policy: shared bytes must match the workspace lockfile, the workspace is never written, and an inapplicable patch is rejected by pnpm.
The manual Windows CI version derives from the product prefix and the UTC run identity, with explicit guidance for an invalid PACKAGE_BUILD_VERSION.
Prepared runtime smoke keeps the payload's progress and termination details on failure and smokes a cross-architecture target without revalidating against the host.
A Python-only native Desktop payload is rejected before any interpreter executes: the payload must declare node and pnpm.
Signs the real PE files of the primary runtime, retains vendor signatures, refuses malformed executables, stops on the first signer failure and audits the final artefact.
The Desktop Web profile keeps exactly one shared MCP resource consumer and a non-disabled webserver entry, with no composition warnings.
The external plugin profile preserves installed packages and the lockfile, disables every third-party bundle, and manages a live/stale owner lock without touching a linked lock target.
Runs the PTC runtime under Electron in both workspace-write and danger-full-access modes, proving the sandbox boundary and that the environment is not inherited.
Quit prompt selection maps task state to one of four prompts, joins an open confirmation instead of stacking a second, and refuses a quit approved after disposal.
The GitHub-Actions key reader masks multiline key bytes and passes the exact fixture to the token action without a shell.
Bilingual pairing record for the desktop tests README.
The shard's orientation document: what the local update verification covers, a layer-by-layer evidence table, and an explicit Open verification list of what is NOT proven.
Chinese version of the desktop local update verification README.
Retains a complete CI release (signed or not) without signing or upload credentials, and refuses to publish a debugging package with rebuild instructions.
The runtime file policy omits development artefacts (.d.ts, maps, tsbuildinfo, native build objects) while keeping executables, assets, licences and native prebuilds.
Shared fixture that materialises a sealed minimal Desktop runtime (five packages plus the Host entry files) for the resource and profile tests.
prepareRuntimeManifests seals dependency metadata that archive preparation would otherwise change, so runtime verification stays stable.
Runtime preparation publishes versions.json only for complete resources; a failed Electron/primary/CLI preparation removes the stale versions file.
A read failure during runtime verification drains the outstanding reads before rejecting and stops scheduling further reads.
Runtime descriptor verification: relocation-independent, integrity-checked only at build time, filesystem links rejected, and nonportable paths refused.
Desktop settings are created on first launch, an older document is defaulted without being rewritten, and an invalid document is reported with its path and left intact.
File-selection policy for the packaged shell against the real electron-builder matchers on both macOS and Windows.
A second process quits without registering lifecycle work; a later launch is routed to the primary process to focus it.
Packs PNG entries into a Vista-style ICO, rejects a bitmap that disagrees with its declared edge, and checks the committed tray icon carries one crisp bitmap per scale.
The tray shows the icon with its tooltip, opens the window on a single click, relabels in the current locale and ignores relabel after disposal.
Update readiness raises one silent system notification (or dock bounce / taskbar flash), returns the user to the confirmation and ignores a stale click.
The update channel is read from the installed channel independently of the current version, defaults to nightly and rejects an unknown channel.

The coordinator checks, downloads on demand and requires a separate installation approval; 100 percent is never readiness, stale download approvals are rejected and late completions after disposal are dropped.
The ordinary update dialog accepts only a displayed choice from its own main frame, follows parent geometry, cancels on abort or disposal, and denies navigation.
Runs the real renderer scripts in JSDOM: diagnostics stay folded and text-only, mandatory diagnostics expand without clearing the block, and server markup renders literally.
The updater's inactivity deadline aborts a request that never receives headers, refreshes on real response bytes, and is removed once the bytes are under verification.
The qualification journal keeps the two installed versions in separate JSONL files, drops detailed errors and unexpected fields instead of redacting them, and refuses relative evidence paths.
The update overlay restores visibility on each parent show, waits for a visible parent and a ready document in either order, and blocks the parent until its last overlay closes.
presentDesktopUpdate records the visible phases, and the error summary is derived from a controlled vocabulary so raw diagnostics never reach a tooltip.
Ordinary polling checks immediately, doubles failed delays up to a cap with jitter, resets after success, starts the delay at completion and never downloads automatically.
The upload command loads the package environment, creates the plan, uploads, and tags the release only after the upload succeeded and only where a tag is required.
The credential launcher uses decrypted credentials only for the matching deployment and bucket, rejects mismatched or malformed ones without printing values, and sanitises both output streams.
The Web document server injects the boot shim, refuses traversal, requires the Host authentication exchange, drops connection-level headers and replaces immutable plugin-bundle caching with no-store.
Built Host acceptance: persists an explicit API key and a browser account login independently across Host restarts.
Onboarding uses authenticated Web RPC, stores only through the configured credential reference, never reads credential values, and rejects malformed keys without contacting a provider.
React welcome page: renders both locales, prevents competing actions, retains an unsaved draft after a refused save, and handles timeout, browser fallback, copy feedback and account expiry notices.
Welcome startup uses the Host before transitioning to the workspace, and never carries update focus into the login or skip path.
The welcome window is fixed-size and sandboxed, blocks renderer navigation, destroys itself when the document fails to load, and accepts actions only from its own top frame.
PE files are unpacked through builder source patterns, an inline PE beside an unpacked copy is rejected, and the archived bytes are verified against the preparation descriptor.
Real console Ctrl events reach asynchronous JavaScript shutdown in Electron Node mode, compiled with the Visual Studio toolchain the test locates itself.
The pinned NSIS template keeps data cleanup out while retaining application removal and registration cleanup, staging before stopping the app and promoting before registering.
Native regression for extraction and directory failure reports: 7-Zip's evidence is kept intact while the dialog headline and excerpt stay bounded.
Native regression proving the installer welcome window is raised above other windows, is not topmost, and records its Presented property.

Deterministic installer progress: a percentage token split across pipe reads still parses, identical work gives the same value on fast and slow disks, and a stalled extractor does not creep to completion.
UIAutomation-driven native installer acceptance over the expected scenario list, using a unique product identity and a private directory.
Adds an InstallerCapture C# helper that enumerates windows, finds text, clicks, and captures screenshots for the native installer checks.
The Windows preset loads unsigned public settings without the signing secret file, resolves secret paths relative to that file, and rejects traversal and deployment mismatch.
Windows-only: the terminal worker is released after a natural exit and after a kill, with stderr required to be empty.
Opt-in Task Scheduler acceptance with an isolated fake runner: disabled task, unlimited execution limit, IgnoreNew policy and restart-count behaviour.
Windows token signing: BAT validation, nested-task signature append, SafeNet command handling, PIN failure stopping the queue, environment scrubbing and NSIS bootstrap signing.
Batch signature parsing rejects missing, duplicate, reordered, extra, null, bad-timestamp and bad-certificate rows, and stderr rejects otherwise complete output.
The Windows signature cache directory is account-local and absolute; a linked or publicly readable cache root is refused, and the execution policy is not changed.
The Windows signature cache reuses verified bytes across targets, distinguishes an avoided signature from an attempted one, and never publishes an entry after a failed verification.

The signing preflight rejects an out-of-period certificate, compiles one probe, verifies one production-format signature, and fails closed on interlock, compiler, certificate, signtool, PIN or audit failures.
Independent signing stages serialise on a stage lock, recheck the cache before touching hardware, and release the handle on failure without releasing another process's lock.
The persistent signing interlock admits one process, retains the slot after that process exits, records both operations, and refuses hardware entry without a supervised run.
Timestamp retries use fresh signed inputs, never publish partial or substituted files, do not retry hardware failures, and retain evidence when attempts are exhausted.
Native uninstall cleanup refuses shell roots, malformed paths and a profile overlapping the target, and removes only the application data it owns.
Production uninstaller acceptance with isolated application identity and seeded data, using the expected scenario list.
Derives the update publisher from a real certificate, escapes DN delimiters for the updater parser, and rejects a missing or ambiguous publisher identity.
